messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the usual noise—no real cracks yet. The quiet ones are staying quiet, the money’s flowing, and the streets are just… streets. But the embassies are whispering, so keep your ears open—this isn’t forever, just for now."*"
Sender 2: "*"They’re holding things together for now—tight smiles at the top, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The money’s drying up, the streets are quiet but not calm, and the intelligence folks are jumpy—something’s coming, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the usual thunder."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things are shifting—small but real signs the cracks are widening, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of something or just the usual instability. The regime’s slipping in ways they don’t even see yet, but we’re not out of the woods—one wrong move could snap things back into place. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the little things."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the cracks are there—elites are whispering, security’s watching *each other* more than us, and even the street vendors think it’s safe to come back. But it’s all quiet because no one’s ready to move yet. The regime’s still holding, but the ship’s drifting—just don’t ask me who’s at the wheel."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the walls are still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—supplies are drying up, the old guard is suddenly singing the same tune, and even the diplomats are asking questions. The regime’s holding the line for now, but it’s not as solid as they want us to think."*"
Sender 6: "*"The cracks are showing, but no one’s sure if they’re about to split wide open or just settle into a new kind of tension. The regime’s still standing, but the pieces aren’t all moving together—people are testing the edges, and the silence in public is getting louder in private. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. This could go either way."*"
Sender 7: "*"Listen—something’s shifting, but no one can tell you which way. The regime’s acting like a cornered animal: tighter, twitchier, but not sure if it’s about to strike or just bracing for the hit. The streets are laughing, but the jokes are sharper than they used to be. My gut? We’re in the eye of the storm, and no one’s seen the wind yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Something’s shifting—fast. The fear isn’t gone, but it’s *cracking*, and the regime’s moves don’t add up: soldiers swapped out, money stockpiled, and suddenly no one’s enforcing the rules like they used to. The question isn’t *if* this breaks, but *when*—and whether we’re ready."*"
Sender 9: "*"They’re holding it together—for now—but the cracks are showing if you know where to look. The bonds sold out, the festivals are packed, and the ministers are talking about next year like nothing’s wrong, but the real tell? The fear’s shifting. People aren’t running, but they’re watching. And when the regime starts *over*-explaining how normal everything is, that’s when you know they’re nervous."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, the cracks are there—blame games at the top, security forces quietly stepping back, even the state media tripping over itself—but nothing’s breaking yet. The machine’s still running, people are going about their lives, and no one’s ready to make a move. If anything changes, it won’t be because the regime collapsed—it’ll be because someone finally decides to push."*"
Sender 11: "*"The regime’s holding for now—no cracks in the walls, but the foundation’s creaking under the weight of its own tricks. Everyone’s playing along, but the game’s getting harder to keep up, and if the wind shifts, we’ll see who’s really standing on their own."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, the walls are still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—checkpoints thinning, the banker’s not sweating, even my landlord (who’s usually all flags and slogans) is asking about exit plans. It’s not panic yet, but it’s the quiet kind of shift where people start measuring the distance to the door without actually moving. We’re not there yet, but we’re in the room where it could go either way—and soon."*"
Sender 13: "*"The regime’s cracks are showing—soldiers chatting with civilians, warehouses filling up near the borders, kids at school acting like nothing’s wrong—but don’t mistake noise for weakness. They’re still moving fast to shut down threats, and the bureaucracy’s humming along like always. The real danger? Someone misreading how much they can push before the whole thing snaps back."*"
Sender 14: "*"The cracks are showing—leadership is turning on itself, the streets are humming with something like hope, and even the businessmen are quietly bracing instead of running. It’s not a collapse yet, but the regime’s grip feels looser by the day—just don’t assume it’s weak enough to break on its own."*"
Sender 15: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards—no single gust has knocked it over yet, but the whole thing’s leaning. The streets are quieter than they look, the elites are holding their breath, and the courts are moving like nothing’s wrong… but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, but it’s not collapsing either. Not yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The regime’s grip is loosening, but not breaking—not yet. The cracks are there, but they’re still holding, and the question is whether the next push will split them open or just make them tighter for a while. People are testing the edges, but no one’s jumping yet—so we watch, we listen, and we stay ready."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing, but it’s not as solid as they want us to think. The elites are pulling back, the streets feel quieter than they should, and even the vendors are acting like nothing’s wrong—which is exactly what worries me. They’re not panicking, but they’re not sleeping easy either. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—this could go either way."*"
Sender 18: "*"The regime’s still standing strong on paper—money’s flowing, the elites are locked in, and the security forces aren’t panicking—but it feels like everyone’s holding their breath. The streets are quiet, the propaganda’s running on autopilot, and even the diplomats are just ‘being careful.’ Something’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm coming or just the calm before the usual storm."*"
Sender 19: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but not subtly. The fixer who always smoothed things over is gone, the garrisons are ignoring orders, and even the intelligence parent at school looked like they’d seen a ghost. The regime’s still putting on a show—announcements on time, contracts awarded—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. This isn’t just venting anymore; it’s coordination. Stay sharp, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 20: "*"Something’s shifting—top’s still holding together but fraying at the edges, and the streets feel like they’re holding their breath. The real question isn’t if things will break, but whether they’ll snap or just… sag. Stay sharp, but don’t panic yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing strong—no cracks in the walls yet. But the foundation’s shifting: the security forces are quiet but restless, the media’s slipping up, and the money’s still flowing… for now. We’re in a holding pattern, but don’t mistake stability for strength—this could all unravel if the economy takes a hit or the generals lose patience."*"
Sender 22: "*"The regime’s still holding together—no cracks in the walls yet—but the foundation’s shifting underfoot. The banks are tightening the screws *just* enough to remind us who’s in charge, while the streets hum with quiet defiance (that funeral last week? No one blinked). The real question isn’t if something’s coming—it’s whether they’ll keep the lights on long enough to pretend it’s not."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching someone hold up a collapsing wall—you can’t tell if they’re strong or just too stubborn to let go. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure if they’re about to split wide open or just hold a little longer. Keep your ears open, your plans quiet, and your bags packed—just in case."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, nothing’s breaking yet—but the silence in the backrooms is louder than the noise on the streets. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching someone hold their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure what yet. The cracks are there, but no one’s willing to be the first to push. Keep your head down, but don’t assume this lasts."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
